scopeNotes: Existing 1492-1783 bounds are not the lifespan of Caddo societies. Removal and modern governmental chronology need further tribal-source work.

phases.label: Regional formation
phases.text: Villages developed ritual centers and mound-and-plaza complexes.

phases.label: Early Caddo
phases.text: Archaeological period within a longer sequence, not a separate sovereign state.

phases.label: Documented local institutions
phases.text: Hasinai observations provide a regional window, not uniform timeless Caddo society.

scopeNotes: Existing 1500-1783 interval is not accepted. This card uses Cherokee Nation history and must not absorb every distinct contemporary Cherokee government. Precolonial town phases and Eastern Band/United Keetoowah histories require separate dossiers.

phases.label: Recorded encounter
phases.text: The Nation dates its first known European contact to the de Soto expedition.

phases.label: Western migrations
phases.text: Some communities moved to Arkansas, then to a treaty-established reservation farther west.

phases.label: Forced removal and rebuilding
phases.text: Forced removal was followed by constitutional reorganization.

scopeNotes: 1492-1500 is an imported map interval, not a lifespan. Confederacy included multiple languages and town histories. Do not move its pre-removal homeland into Oklahoma. OHS has geographic and early-chronology problems outside the narrowly used claims.

phases.label: Confederacy transformation
phases.text: Town amalgamation, population movement and trade shaped the confederacy.

phases.label: Removal and government
phases.text: Forced relocation preceded national governmental reorganization.

phases.label: Constitutional phase
phases.text: Constitution and Okmulgee capital mark institutional transformation.

scopeNotes: Inherited 1492-1715 ends before documented Natchez institutions. No exact fell-to year approved. Earlier archaeological ancestry around 700 is not an exact ethnic founding. Refugee communities are continuation relationships, not conquering successors.

phases.label: Mound construction
phases.text: Grand Village construction accumulated in stages.

phases.label: Documented ceremonial center
phases.text: Site prominence is not the lifetime of all Natchez communities.

phases.label: Dispersal
phases.text: French defeat and displacement led to refugee movements, not extinction.

scopeNotes: 1492-1500 is not a Mapuche lifespan. Wallmapu is not validated here as a single sovereign polygon. Source dates Araucania incorporation 1882; conflicting conventional 1883 chronology remains unresolved, so no exact fall date used. Indigenous-author scholarship and textiles remain next work.

phases.label: Colonial resistance
phases.text: A major rebellion expelled Spanish settlers from Mapuche-held territory.

phases.label: Frontier transformations
phases.text: Commerce and Pampas connections reshaped social life.

phases.label: Republican occupation
phases.text: Separate Chilean and Argentine campaigns require region-specific chronologies.

phases.label: Reduction regime
phases.text: Imposed land arrangements altered kinship and access to resources.

scopeNotes: Do not equate Arawak language family, earlier archaeological cultures and Taíno political identity. No unified state borders or universal 1500 extinction accepted. Island-specific chiefdom chronology remains to research.

phases.label: Cultural formation
phases.text: The Berkeley teaching chronology distinguishes Taíno development from earlier Caribbean sequences.

phases.label: Colonization
phases.text: Disease, famine and enslavement disrupted communities.

phases.label: Living heritage
phases.text: Language and culture revitalization contradict a simple disappearance narrative.

scopeNotes: Specific Mbya scope, not all Guarani or colonial mission populations. Single scholarly institutional synthesis so far; independent complementary Indigenous source required. Early ethnogenesis and colonial transformations remain unresolved.

phases.label: Land recognition
phases.text: A São Paulo agreement led to recognition of specified village lands, not a universal Guarani border.

phases.label: Institutional adaptation
phases.dateDescription: mid 1990s onward, as described in early 2000s
phases.text: Political and spiritual roles increasingly separated.

scopeNotes: Duplicate existing totonaco needs resolution. 1492-1500 is not accepted as a cultural lifespan. El Tajin ethnicity disputed, so its archaeological claims are not imported wholesale. INAH Cempoala text incorrectly places Toltec pressure in 900 BCE; excluded. Institution dates and modern Indigenous-authored source remain pending.

phases.label: Tributary transformation
phases.text: Cempoala collected tribute under Mexica domination.

phases.label: Colonial alliance
phases.text: Cempoala's alliance was a particular political decision, not the end of every Totonac society.

scopeNotes: No exact existing ID found. Two complementary sources checked. Conquest and negotiated rule still need specific 1522/1530 evidence. INAH attributes founding 1325 to Tariacuri, not accepted as exact state founding. Pohl has an area conversion error, excluded. No supported fell-to link yet.

phases.label: Regional emergence
phases.text: Pohl places the emergence of regional Tarascan dominance around this time.

phases.label: Later regional state
phases.text: INAH's regional presentation places a flourishing Tarascan kingdom around 1450.

scopeNotes: Existing mixtecs 800-1000 identity interval is inadequate. Do not conflate mixtec-empire 1279-1530 with all peoples. Specific Tilantongo/Tlaxiaco phase identities require separate registry entries. Colonial pictorial continuation is supported; contemporary Indigenous governments and complete conquest histories still need sources.

phases.label: Genealogical memory
phases.text: The manuscript recounts regional royal families across this span.

phases.label: Tilantongo succession dispute
phases.text: Bodley is read as depicting displacement of Two Earthquake's line. This concerns Tilantongo, not all Mixtec communities.

phases.label: Tlaxiaco confrontation
phases.text: Pohl reports Jimenez Moreno's identification of Eight Grass with a Tlaxiaco lord killed in conflict with the Aztecs.

scopeNotes: The imported name toltec-empire presupposes an imperial identity under debate. 1279 endpoint not source-checked. Pohl's separate overview extends power into thirteenth century, conflicting with site 1150 endpoint; require INAH stratigraphic chronology. Do not adopt museum's pan-Mesoamerican conquest or earliest militarism claims.

phases.label: Urban period
phases.dateDescription: approximately 800-1150 CE in Pohl's site account
phases.text: Site-level chronology is provisional, not a verified empire lifespan.

phases.label: Later memory
phases.text: Quetzalcoatl narratives attached prestige to ancient Tula.

checks: Every claim and phase source key resolves
At least four substantive items per card
Card hashes recorded for subsequent independent review
